story.iWant: to set up a Next.js project with TypeScript and core dependencies
story.soThat: I have a clean foundation to build the application
story.tasks:
- [ ] Task 1: Create Next.js Project (AC: 1) - [ ] Run `npx create-next-app@latest will-it-rain --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app` - [ ] Verify Next.js 15+ installed with App Router - [ ] Verify TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and ESLint configured
- [ ] Task 2: Configure TypeScript Strict Mode (AC: 1) - [ ] Update `tsconfig.json` to enable `"strict": true` - [ ] Configure path aliases (`"@/*": ["./*"]`) - [ ] Verify TypeScript compiler settings match architecture spec
- [ ] Task 3: Initialize Git Repository (AC: 1) - [ ] Run `git init` - [ ] Create `.gitignore` for Node.js/Next.js projects - [ ] Verify `.env.local` is in `.gitignore` - [ ] Make initial commit with project setup
- [ ] Task 4: Verify Project Structure (AC: 1) - [ ] Confirm `app/` directory exists (App Router) - [ ] Confirm `public/` directory exists - [ ] Confirm `package.json` with correct dependencies - [ ] Confirm `next.config.js` present - [ ] Confirm `tailwind.config.ts` present
- [ ] Task 5: Test Development Server (AC: 1) - [ ] Run `npm install` to ensure all dependencies installed - [ ] Run `npm run dev` and verify server starts on localhost:3000 - [ ] Verify no TypeScript compilation errors - [ ] Verify landing page loads in browser
- [ ] Task 6: Create Basic README (AC: 1) - [ ] Document project description: "Will It Rain - Simple 24-hour rain forecast" - [ ] Include setup instructions for development - [ ] Note Node.js 18+ requirement

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** a greenfield project environment **When** I initialize the project **Then** a Next.js project with App Router is created with TypeScript configuration **And** essential dependencies are installed (React, Next.js, TypeScript) **And** the project structure follows Next.js conventions (app/, public/, etc.) **And** TypeScript is configured with strict mode enabled **And** the development server runs successfully on localhost

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Foundation & Infrastructure
doc.snippet: Epic 1 establishes the technical foundation for Will It Rain by initializing the Next.js 15 project with TypeScript, configuring the styling system (Tailwind CSS v4 + Shadcn UI), setting up environment management for API keys, configuring basic PWA capabilities, and establishing development tooling.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Foundation & Infrastructure
doc.snippet: Framework: Next.js 15 with App Router (ADR-001), Language: TypeScript with strict mode, Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 + Shadcn UI (ADR-006), Deployment Target: Vercel (ADR-007), Build Tool: Turbopack (dev), Webpack (prod).

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Foundation & Infrastructure
doc.snippet: Runtime Dependencies: next ^15.0.0, react ^18.3.0, react-dom ^18.3.0. Development Dependencies: typescript ^5.3.0, @types/node ^20.10.0, @types/react ^18.2.0, @types/react-dom ^18.2.0, tailwindcss ^4.0.0.

doc.title: Architecture
doc.snippet: Decision: Use Next.js 15 with App Router architecture. Rationale: Native PWA support (manifest.ts added in fall 2024), Serverless API routes perfect for single `/api/check-rain` endpoint, Vercel deployment optimization (zero config), App Router is the future (Pages Router in maintenance mode).

doc.title: Architecture
doc.snippet: Create Next.js project with all dependencies using: npx create-next-app@latest will-it-rain --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app. This establishes the base architecture with: Next.js 15 with App Router, TypeScript for type safety, Tailwind CSS v4 for styling, ESLint for code quality.

doc.title: Architecture
doc.snippet: will-it-rain/ includes: app/ (layout.tsx root layout, page.tsx landing page, globals.css Tailwind directives, manifest.ts PWA manifest), components/ (ui/ for Shadcn UI components), lib/ (utils.ts, openweather.ts, rain-logic.ts), public/ (icons/, favicon.ico).

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: The MVP delivers the complete core experience: one question, one answer, radical simplicity. Progressive Web App (PWA): Installable on all platforms (iOS, Android, desktop), Works in browser or as installed app, Responsive design: mobile, tablet, desktop.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: NFR-P1: Page Load Performance - Initial page load (landing page): < 1 second, Time to Interactive (TTI): < 1.5 seconds, First Contentful Paint (FCP): < 0.8 seconds. Lighthouse Performance score > 90.

doc.title: UX Design Specification
doc.snippet: Selected System: Shadcn UI + Tailwind CSS v4. Rationale: Radix UI primitives provide unstyled, accessible components as base, Tailwind CSS v4 provides latest styling tooling for efficient customization, Copy-paste architecture means components owned by the project and fully customizable.

development.package: TypeScript compiler with strict mode support

frameworks.framework: Next.js 15 App Router - Full-stack React framework
Tailwind CSS v4 - Utility-first CSS framework

versionConstraints.constraint: Next.js 15.0.0 or higher (required for native PWA support)

constraint.rule: Next.js 15 with App Router architecture (ADR-001) - App Router is mandatory, Pages Router not supported
Strict mode required - No exceptions. Configure tsconfig.json with "strict": true, "target": "ES2017", "lib": ["dom", "dom.iterable", "esnext"], Path alias: "@/*": ["./*"]
ESLint rule: No `any` types allowed. All TypeScript must be strictly typed.
Turbopack for development (Next.js 15 default), Webpack for production builds. No additional configuration needed.
File-based routing in app/ directory. Server Components by default. Must follow Next.js 15 App Router conventions.
NFR-P1: Dev server startup < 3 seconds. Initial page load < 1 second. Lighthouse Performance score > 90.

tests.standards: For Epic 1 (Foundation), no automated tests are required yet. Configuration is validated through successful builds and manual verification. Testing infrastructure (Jest + React Testing Library, Playwright for E2E) will be deferred to Epic 5. Current validation approach: ensure dev server starts without errors, TypeScript compiles cleanly (tsc --noEmit), and landing page loads successfully at localhost:3000.

testIdea.description: Verify TypeScript strict mode is enabled in tsconfig.json
testIdea.approach: Manual verification: Check tsconfig.json contains "strict": true

testIdea.description: Validate Next.js 15 App Router is correctly configured
testIdea.approach: Manual verification: Run npm run dev, verify server starts on localhost:3000, check that app/ directory exists with layout.tsx and page.tsx

testIdea.description: Ensure all essential dependencies are installed
testIdea.approach: Manual verification: Check package.json for react ^18.3.0, next ^15.0.0, typescript ^5.3.0, and verify npm install completes without errors
Manual verification: Run tsc --noEmit and verify no compilation errors

testIdea.description: Verify landing page renders in browser
testIdea.approach: Manual verification: Open localhost:3000 in browser after running npm run dev, confirm page loads without errors
